environment.reference_runtime: Bun-compiled ELF binary at /root/.opencode/bin/opencode (bun/node toolchain absent; reference source not directly executable)

findings.title: Zero production cross-crate integration: the executable wires none of the domain crates
evidence: grep 'use oc_' crates/*/src => 0 matches in production source (coordinator re-verified)
266 'TODO(integration)' markers; 17 files contain 'not yet wired' (coordinator re-verified)
Every crate declares sibling deps in Cargo.toml but none import them
findings.impact: No end-to-end workflow functions. All domain crates compile and test in isolation but are never reached by the binary. The port is 20 tested silos, not an application.
findings.root_cause: The parallel worktree build produced isolated, mutually-dependent-by-declaration crates; the integration/wiring phase (oc-cli calling into oc-server/oc-session/oc-llm/oc-tool/oc-database/oc-plugin/oc-tui) was never performed.
findings.recommended_remediation: Phase 1 integration: implement oc-cli wiring to oc-server::Server::listen, LocalClient over the real router, oc-session/oc-session-runner over real stores, and promote canonical types to oc-schema (remove 266 mirror markers).
recommended_tests: End-to-end integration test that runs the real binary against a mock provider and asserts a full session round trip.

findings.title: `opencode run` (headless) is dead: exits 1 with 'in-process opencode server is not wired yet'
evidence: timeout 20 ./target/release/opencode run 'hi' => 'Error:  the in-process opencode server is not wired yet in this build (TODO(integration): oc-server)', exit 1 (coordinator re-verified). Reference exits 0 and prints a response.
findings.impact: Primary headless workflow of the product is non-functional. A mock OpenAI endpoint receives zero HTTP requests from the Rust binary.
findings.root_cause: LocalClient::create always returns the not-wired error; the in-process server path was never connected.
findings.recommended_remediation: Wire LocalClient over oc_server router + oc-session/oc-session-runner/oc-llm/oc-tool.
recommended_tests: End-to-end `opencode run` against a mock SSE provider asserting streaming output.

findings.title: `opencode serve` is a bare TCP socket, not an HTTP server
evidence: serve --port 43199: curl /api/health => HTTP 000 (coordinator re-verified). Static: the only oc_server reference in oc-cli is a TODO comment (serve.rs:38).
findings.impact: No server API, SSE, WebSocket, or attach target. Clients hang. oc-server's real axum router is never mounted.
findings.root_cause: serve.rs binds a TcpListener and discards bytes instead of calling oc_server::Server::listen.
findings.recommended_remediation: Mount oc_server router in the serve command with proper shutdown.
recommended_tests: HTTP integration test: /api/health, /api/session, /api/event over a live serve process.

findings.title: Default TUI, --mini, and attach are stubs
evidence: `opencode` with no args under a real pty => 'Error: the TUI is not yet wired in this build (TODO(integration): oc-tui)', exit 1. oc_tui::app::run_async has zero callers in the workspace.
findings.impact: Interactive use of the product is impossible.
findings.root_cause: TUI launch seam never connected; non-TTY fallback prints 'starting TUI (requires a TTY)' and exits.
findings.recommended_remediation: Wire oc-cli default command to oc_tui::app::run_async with server-backed client.
recommended_tests: PTY-driven launch test asserting TUI first frame renders.

findings.title: The production executable never opens the database; nothing persists across restarts
evidence: Database::open has zero non-test call sites; no crate outside oc-database references oc_database:: symbols. Server uses in-memory Stores; event bus uses InMemoryDurableStore. Runtime: `opencode db "SELECT 1"` => 'not yet wired', exit 1.
reproduction: grep -rn 'oc_database::' crates/*/src | grep -v oc-database | wc -l => 0; ./target/release/opencode db 'SELECT 1'
findings.impact: Sessions, messages, events, and credentials are never persisted; no crash recovery, no resume after restart.
findings.root_cause: DB-backed commands stubbed; no production caller of Database::open.
findings.recommended_remediation: Wire Database::open into oc-server stores and session storage; implement session/export/import commands over it.
recommended_tests: Restart-persistence test: create session, restart binary, list session.

findings.title: Session list/delete, export, and import commands are 'not yet wired'
evidence: `opencode session list` => 'Error:  session listing is not yet wired in this build (TODO(integration): oc-database/oc-session)', exit 1 (coordinator re-verified).
findings.impact: Session lifecycle management unusable.
findings.recommended_remediation: Implement over oc-database.

findings.title: No MCP/ACP/client wire path is reachable from the executable; mcp/acp commands are stubs; MCP protocol version is stale
evidence: `opencode acp` binds a socket and pending()s (zero bytes); `opencode mcp list` returns not_wired. oc-mcp advertises protocolVersion 2025-06-18; the reference binary sends 2025-11-25. Configured mock MCP server never spawned.
findings.impact: MCP/ACP integrations non-functional; protocol-version negotiation would reject current reference peers.
findings.root_cause: Wire crates unreachable + stale version constants + golden fixtures encoding the stale version.
findings.recommended_remediation: Wire MCP/ACP into server/cli; update protocolVersion to reference; regenerate fixtures from reference capture.
recommended_tests: Live MCP round-trip via production executable; version negotiation test vs reference.

findings.title: Tool approval gate is not enforced: model tool calls execute without user approval
evidence: ToolContext::ask and CoreContext::assert only push to a Vec and return Ok; the server permission handler returns effect:'allow' unconditionally. oc-tool write test demonstrates an unapproved write. Coordinator re-verified the source.
findings.impact: A prompt-injected repository can make the model run arbitrary commands and write arbitrary files with zero approval once the tool loop is wired. Defeats opencode's core safety control.
findings.root_cause: Approval hooks are record-only; no allow/ask/deny evaluation path exists.
findings.recommended_remediation: Implement a real permission service (allow/ask/deny rule evaluation + server prompt round trip) and bind it to tool execution.
recommended_tests: Approval denial test: deny rule must block bash execution; ask rule must require server confirmation.

findings.title: PTY connect ticket is never validated; auth bypass on the PTY WebSocket
evidence: Auth middleware skips any /api/pty/*/connect?ticket=x; handler accepts any non-empty ticket; token shape is 'ticket_{len}'. Reference uses a random single-use UUID ticket.
findings.impact: Unauthenticated interactive shell access once the server is reachable.
findings.root_cause: Ticket generation/validation simplified to a stub.
findings.recommended_remediation: Random single-use ticket with server-side cache validation.

findings.title: v1 /file/content containment guard dropped (arbitrary file read)
evidence: The reference's FSUtil.contains containment check is absent from the Rust handler.
findings.impact: Once the server is reachable, any authenticated (or unauthenticated if no password) client can read arbitrary files.
findings.recommended_remediation: Restore workspace-containment check on all fs handlers.
recommended_tests: File-read traversal test outside the workspace.

findings.title: Tool execution is unreachable from the executable; permission enforcement entirely missing
evidence: RunnerDeps/ToolRegistry/ToolSettle have no production impls; RunnerDeps constructed only in tests. No path exists for model output to execute commands (currently safe only because the loop is dead).
findings.impact: Agentic tool loop is test-only; when wired without remediation, model tool calls run unapproved (SEC-001).
findings.recommended_remediation: Wire runner + tool registry + permission enforcement together.

findings.title: Read tools buffer the entire file before pagination (OOM on large files)
evidence: std::fs::read on the whole file before pagination; reference streams and stops at the byte cap.
findings.impact: Multi-GB file read -> OOM.
findings.root_cause: Whole-file read instead of capped streaming.
findings.recommended_remediation: Stream up to the byte cap like the reference.

findings.title: Symlink-following workspace escape; containment is lexical
evidence: Probe wrote through ws/link/evil.txt into a directory outside the workspace without external_directory approval.
findings.impact: Write outside the workspace via symlink.
findings.root_cause: Lexical path check; symlink_metadata follows intermediate links.
findings.recommended_remediation: Resolve symlinks and re-check containment; or deny writes through symlinks.

findings.title: Shell timeout/abort kills only the direct child, not the process group
evidence: sh -c 'sleep 1000 &' orphans grandchildren on timeout.
findings.impact: Runaway processes after shell timeout.
findings.recommended_remediation: Start in a new process group and kill the group.

findings.title: No QuickJS memory limit, interrupt handler, or watchdog: plugin infinite loops hang the process
evidence: JS_SetMemoryLimit/JS_SetInterruptHandler never called; a plugin for(;;){} hung the process (killed at 15s); unfulfillable await busy-spins forever.
findings.impact: Malicious or buggy plugin = DoS / frozen agent.
findings.root_cause: No runtime limits or interrupt hook.
findings.recommended_remediation: Set memory limit + interrupt handler with timeout; add a watchdog.
recommended_tests: Plugin infinite-loop and memory-blowup timeout tests.

findings.title: Plugins can read and execute arbitrary local JS (no module-path containment)
evidence: ModuleResolver accepts absolute specs with no containment; runtime-proven import of /tmp/.../evil.js outside the plugin dir.
findings.impact: A plugin can read/execute arbitrary local files beyond its directory.
findings.root_cause: Missing path containment on module resolution.
findings.recommended_remediation: Restrict module resolution to the plugin dir + allowed node_modules; sandbox host functions.

findings.title: event hooks silently dropped; async polyfill limitations break real plugins
evidence: event hooks schedule a microtask never pumped; integration test asserts nothing observable. Timer-based I/O hangs (setTimeout runs on next tick only).
findings.impact: Plugins relying on event hooks or real async I/O misbehave.
findings.root_cause: No event-loop pumping for host-queued microtasks.
findings.recommended_remediation: Pump host-queued microtasks; provide a real event loop bridge.

findings.title: Plugin runtime is TEST-ONLY: no production caller; `opencode plugin` returns 'not yet implemented'
evidence: PluginBuilder/LoadedPlugin used only by tests/examples; no PluginHost impl outside tests.
findings.impact: Plugin feature not delivered.
findings.recommended_remediation: Wire plugin host into server/cli after PLUGIN-001/002 fixes.
recommended_tests: End-to-end plugin load + hook execution via the binary.

findings.title: unwrap() panics inside the extern "C" trampoline (unwind across FFI) when a JS exception contains NUL
evidence: new Error('\u0000') or Rust callback returning NUL-laden text triggers panic inside the trampoline.
findings.impact: Undefined behavior / process abort from a plugin-controlled string.
findings.root_cause: panic inside extern C without catch_unwind.
findings.recommended_remediation: Wrap trampoline bodies in catch_unwind and map to a JS error.

findings.title: Unbounded recursion on self-referential arrays causes stack overflow
evidence: a.push(a) recurses infinitely; the visited cycle set covers objects but not arrays.
findings.impact: Process abort from a plugin constructing a self-referential array.
findings.recommended_remediation: Include arrays in the visited set.

findings.title: Negative/Proxy-spoofed array length triggers a large property-read loop (CPU DoS)
evidence: 0..2^32 property-read loop on spoofed length.
findings.impact: CPU exhaustion from a plugin.
findings.recommended_remediation: Cap array conversion size.

findings.title: RunCoordinator lost-wakeup race can hang waiters permanently
evidence: Stress harness reproduced a hang in 2/3 runs with concurrent waiters; single-waiter never hangs. Zero unit tests for the coordinator.
findings.impact: Session runs hang indefinitely under concurrency.
findings.root_cause: Waiter checks result then awaits Notify::notified(); notify_waiters can fire in between.
findings.recommended_remediation: Use a condition-variable style wait (re-check under lock) or Notified guard that re-checks.

findings.title: run_future blocks within an async task ('Cannot start a runtime from within a runtime')
evidence: Handle::block_on from within an async task panics; every tool path (bash/webfetch/misc) hits this once wired into the runner.
findings.impact: Panic on first tool execution once the loop is wired.
findings.root_cause: One-shot runtime used inside an existing runtime.
findings.recommended_remediation: Detect ambient runtime and run inline, or restructure to always await.
recommended_tests: Tool execution from within a tokio runtime.

findings.title: Runner buffers the entire provider turn; no incremental streaming; cancellation drops the turn
evidence: Events publish only after the whole turn; reference streams token-by-token and persists partial output; cancel drops the buffered turn. Unbounded memory on long streams.
findings.impact: No incremental UX, no partial persistence, memory growth, wrong interruption semantics.
findings.root_cause: Buffered Vec<LLMEvent> instead of a real stream.
findings.recommended_remediation: Expose a real stream from oc-llm and publish incrementally.

findings.title: HTTP interrupt endpoint never reaches the runner
evidence: /session/:id/interrupt only flips record.active; no path reaches RunCoordinator::interrupt/CancellationToken.
findings.impact: User-initiated interrupts do nothing.
findings.recommended_remediation: Connect interrupt handler to cancellation token.

findings.title: Usage/cost accounting undercounts cached tokens (dead metadata fallbacks)
evidence: Reference anthropic/vertex/bedrock/venice cache-write fallbacks never consulted; cacheWrite undercounted, input overcharged.
findings.impact: Incorrect token/cost reporting.
findings.recommended_remediation: Port the fallback chain.

findings.title: Retry jitter is deterministic and can exceed MAX_DELAY; HTTP-date Retry-After dropped
evidence: base*0.8+(attempt*37)%20 vs reference uniform random; can exceed MAX_DELAY.
findings.impact: Minor divergence in backoff behavior.
findings.recommended_remediation: Use a real random jitter bounded by MAX_DELAY; parse HTTP-date Retry-After.

findings.title: config parser accepts inputs the reference rejects (json5 vs jsonc-parser)
evidence: Single-quoted strings and unquoted keys accepted by Rust, rejected by the reference.
findings.impact: Configs invalid per spec silently accepted.
findings.root_cause: json5 crate is more permissive than jsonc-parser.
findings.recommended_remediation: Replace with a jsonc-parser-equivalent implementation.

findings.title: Config load error handling diverges (whitespace-only file, dir-as-config, legacy TOML over-validation)
evidence: Whitespace-only config returns defaults (reference errors ValueExpected); non-ENOENT read errors swallowed as defaults; legacy TOML unknown keys abort migration.
findings.impact: Silent acceptance of broken configs; failed migrations.
findings.recommended_remediation: Mirror reference error semantics.

findings.title: attach SSE parser drops events after the first per network chunk
evidence: Closure-local buffer discarded on return; two text events in one chunk => no output, exit 0; per-event delays => both print.
findings.impact: Silently lost streaming output on fast servers.
findings.recommended_remediation: Persist the SSE buffer across events.

findings.title: v1 /event heartbeat is an SSE comment, not the reference server.heartbeat event; SSE frame format diverges
evidence: Rust emits 'event: message\ndata: ...'; live reference emits bare 'data: {...}' with ': heartbeat'. Missing location filtering and server.instance.disposed termination.
findings.impact: SSE consumers expecting reference framing break.
findings.recommended_remediation: Match reference framing byte-for-byte; regenerate fixtures from captured reference bytes.
recommended_tests: SSE framing golden test vs captured reference stream.

findings.title: Published performance claims compare unequal workloads
evidence: Stock --version/--help boot Bun/V8 and evaluate the full module graph; Rust short-circuits at clap parse before the runtime builds. Neither loads config/plugins (poisoned-config probe). Published 981ms/185MB stock numbers not reproduced (1126-2036ms, 175-201MB measured); 7ms Rust figure inflated by shell overhead (true exec ~2ms).
findings.impact: The '140x/46x' claims are directionally real (runtime-boot elimination) but not equivalent-work speedups; misleading as published. RSS ~38-40x, timing ~72-820x depending on warm/cold; 23x binary size reproduced.
findings.root_cause: Benchmark methodology compares time-to-answer for paths doing different work.
findings.recommended_remediation: Benchmark equivalent-work scenarios (config load, server startup, session round-trip) and document the workload caveat.

findings.title: No test invokes the real executable; zero binary/E2E/differential coverage
evidence: No CARGO_BIN_EXE, no target/release reference, no reference-binary invocation anywhere; oc-cli has no integration tests and 21 units.
findings.impact: The 1519 passing tests prove crate-level behavior only; none prove the product works.
findings.recommended_remediation: Add binary + differential test harness (golden against reference executable).

findings.title: oc-session / oc-session-runner test only local mirror types; cross-crate wire consistency unproven
evidence: oc-session and oc-session-runner declare deps on oc-schema/oc-llm/oc-tool but reference none; tests validate only the mirrors.
findings.impact: Duplicate types may diverge; integration will need reconciliation.
findings.recommended_remediation: Promote canonical types to oc-schema and re-test.

findings.title: Some golden fixtures are hand-written or contradict the reference
evidence: oc-llm 'recorded cassette' bodies hand-written (prompt differs from cassette); oc-tool task golden asserts a schema without background, contradicting the cited reference snapshot.
findings.impact: Golden tests can pin divergences instead of parity.
findings.root_cause: Fixtures authored by hand, not captured from reference.
findings.recommended_remediation: Capture fixtures from the reference binary/recordings.

findings.title: Several high-risk paths are mutation-proof (no test would catch regressions)
evidence: GoUsageLimitError retry branch, runner interruption handling, WebSocket/pty upgrade, and the entire TUI app have no failing-test guard.
findings.impact: Regressions in critical paths go undetected.
findings.recommended_remediation: Add targeted tests for the mutation-proof paths.
recommended_tests: Targeted unit tests for each listed path.

findings.title: Terminal escape injection: markdown renderer passes raw ANSI/OSC sequences through
evidence: Harness flushed \x1b[31mred\x1b[0m\x1b]0;TITLE\x07 through Terminal::draw; SGR and OSC sequences pass through (ratatui Span::render_ref).
findings.impact: Malicious model output can spoof UI, run OSC-based terminal attacks.
findings.recommended_remediation: Sanitize/escape control sequences in rendered text (filter via set_stringn or explicit csi handling).

findings.title: No terminal restoration on panic/SIGTERM/SIGHUP
evidence: Raw mode + alt screen restored only on the happy path; no panic hook, no signal handler.
findings.impact: Broken terminal after crash/kill.
findings.recommended_remediation: Panic hook + signal handlers restoring terminal state.

findings.title: 58 of 183 keybindings dispatch to no-ops
evidence: diff viewer keys, which-key, terminal.suspend, MCP/plugin dialogs fall through; Route has only Home/Session.
findings.impact: Advertised UI actions silently do nothing.
findings.recommended_remediation: Wire or remove no-op bindings.

findings.title: Plugin engine ships a 7-year-old QuickJS (2019-07-21) that executes untrusted JS; upstream moved to QuickJS-ng
evidence: crates.io libquickjs-sys 0.1.0 compiles the bundled 2019 snapshot via make; upstream uses QuickJS-ng 0.4+. Specific CVEs unverified (cargo-audit unavailable).
findings.impact: Unmaintained C engine executing plugin JS; unknown vulns; build needs make/gcc/ar.
findings.recommended_remediation: Upgrade to a maintained QuickJS (quickjs-ng / boa) with active maintenance.
recommended_tests: Engine upgrade CI + plugin compat suite.

findings.title: Cargo.lock is gitignored and untracked; builds are non-reproducible
evidence: git ls-files | grep Cargo.lock => empty; fresh checkouts re-resolve latest semver.
findings.impact: No reproducible/offline/--locked builds.
findings.recommended_remediation: Commit Cargo.lock.

findings.title: MIT attribution violation: no LICENSE file; embedded reference content without copyright notice
evidence: Port declares license = 'MIT' but ships no LICENSE; embeds verbatim reference prompts/polyfill/model catalog without the required copyright notice.
findings.impact: Legal risk on redistribution; violates the MIT reference's attribution requirement.
findings.recommended_remediation: Add LICENSE (MIT, with upstream copyright notice) and per-asset attribution.

findings.title: No release-profile hardening (no LTO/strip/panic=abort)
evidence: Binary unstripped 8.05MB; codegen-units=16; panic=unwind; measured stripped size ~31x smaller than stock.
findings.impact: Larger binaries; no panic-abort hardening.
findings.recommended_remediation: Add [profile.release] with lto=true, strip=true, panic=abort (after auditing panic paths).

findings.title: No logging subsystem: --print-logs/--log-level are no-ops; reference always writes opencode.log
evidence: No tracing subscriber anywhere; log file byte-identical after --print-logs; no stderr output.
findings.impact: No diagnosability; operational blind spot.
findings.recommended_remediation: Install a tracing subscriber honoring --print-logs/--log-level; write opencode.log.

findings.title: Hardcoded version 1.18.13 (crate is 0.1.0); binary indistinguishable from upstream
evidence: --version prints 1.18.13 from a hardcoded constant; crate version is 0.1.0.
findings.impact: Version confusion; can't distinguish this port from upstream.
findings.recommended_remediation: Inject a distinct port version (e.g. 0.1.0-opencode-1.18.13) via build metadata.

findings.title: upgrade is a stub with no signature verification and wrong upstream; uninstall doesn't remove the binary
evidence: Fetches latest from sst/opencode (reference queries anomalyco/opencode), never installs, --method ignored, no signatures/checksums, exit 0. Uninstall removes data dirs but not the binary.
findings.impact: Update channel is fake; uninstall leaves the binary.
findings.recommended_remediation: Implement signed updates and full uninstall.

findings.title: No CI, no installer, no packaging, no prebuilt binaries, no SBOM/signing
evidence: No .github/ directory; no release workflow; no packaging targets.
findings.impact: Cannot distribute or CI-verify the product.
findings.recommended_remediation: Add CI (build/clippy/test on Linux/macOS/Windows) and a release pipeline with SBOM.

findings.title: Event-bus subscriber lists never remove dead senders (unbounded growth)
evidence: Subscriber lists and durable_wakes never remove dead senders; O(leaked) per-commit wake cost.
findings.impact: Long-running memory growth.
findings.recommended_remediation: Remove closed senders.

findings.title: Orphaned subprocesses on timeout; kill-on-drop missing in several process paths
evidence: tokio kill_on_drop=false without Drop guard; MCP stdio children leak on drop.
findings.impact: Runaway child processes.
findings.recommended_remediation: Set kill_on_drop / add Drop guards.

findings.title: Unbounded shell-output capture and MCP SSE buffer (memory DoS)
evidence: read_to_end then truncate in bash; unbounded MCP SSE buffer + unbounded channels.
findings.impact: Memory exhaustion from large outputs/malicious MCP server.
findings.recommended_remediation: Bound captures and channel capacities.

findings.title: Blocking operations inside the async executor (rg/fs/sqlite in async paths)
evidence: Sync tool handlers run rg/fs synchronously in the async loop; blocking npm install latent.
findings.impact: Runtime stalls.
findings.recommended_remediation: spawn_blocking for CPU/IO-heavy work.

findings.title: JSON-mode columns store primitive values raw, not JSON-stringified; db path ignores OPENCODE_CHANNEL
evidence: Runtime: prompt='hello' stored raw as hello, breaking read-back parse; `opencode db path` prints opencode.db under canary, ignoring OPENCODE_CHANNEL/OPENCODE_DISABLE_CHANNEL_DB.
findings.impact: Data read-back breaks; wrong channel DB selection.
findings.root_cause: JSON column handling + channel logic not wired.
findings.recommended_remediation: JSON-stringify JSON-mode columns; honor channel env vars in the CLI command.
recommended_tests: JSON column round-trip test; channel path test.

findings.title: Systematic stream/format divergences (stdout vs stderr, broken pipe, error spacing, repeated flags)
evidence: Reference tables go to stdout, Rust to stderr; ui::error adds a double space; broken pipe exits 1 with an error vs reference silent exit 0; repeated flags rejected; --get-yargs-completions missing.
findings.impact: Script-compatibility divergences.
findings.recommended_remediation: Align output streams, error formatting, broken-pipe handling.

findings.title: MCP clientInfo.version is 0.1.0, not the install version
evidence: clientInfo.version uses crate version 0.1.0; reference sends InstallationVersion.
findings.impact: Wire identity divergence.
findings.recommended_remediation: Share the workspace version.

findings.title: Config side-effect divergences (tools key removed, non-canonical plugin URLs)
evidence: Rust removes the tools key after deriving permission (reference retains it); emits file:///..././local-plugin instead of normalized URL.
findings.impact: Plugin identity and config round-trip diverge.
findings.recommended_remediation: Mirror reference key retention and URL normalization.

findings.title: Invariant panics reachable on user-triggerable paths (llm.rs:214, shell_prompt.rs:70)
evidence: invariant!/unwrap on parse assumptions that malformed input could violate.
findings.impact: Crash on malformed input.
findings.recommended_remediation: Convert to error returns.

findings.title: Benchmark methodology noise: 'cold-start' mislabeled, max-not-median RSS, shell overhead
evidence: compare.sh never drops caches (published 981ms is warm); true cold stock 1984ms vs rust 27ms (~72x); RSS max-not-median.
findings.impact: Published numbers not reproducible as stated.
findings.recommended_remediation: Report median with cold/warm split and equivalent-work scenarios.

findings.title: Runtime external-binary dependencies (ripgrep auto-download, git, unzip, tar) with no offline story
evidence: ripgrep binary auto-download at runtime; git/unzip/tar assumed present; Windows shell fallback gap.
findings.impact: Offline/enterprise environments break.
findings.recommended_remediation: Bundle or document required external binaries; offline fallbacks.

findings.title: Canonical oc-schema types unused; identical types duplicated 2-8x across crates
evidence: Message x8, SessionInfo x7, ModelRef x7, Entry x7 duplicated; oc-schema's Message referenced only by its own golden test.
findings.impact: Divergence risk; maintenance burden; integration cost.
findings.recommended_remediation: Promote canonical types; delete mirrors.

findings.title: 47 'not yet wired' call sites across commands; many commands parse but exit 1
affected_components: oc-cli commands: completion, mcp, session, db, stats, export, import, agent, github, console, plugin, generate, debug
evidence: COMMAND-COMPATIBILITY.csv: 148 rows, only 17 equivalent (11.5%); 43 rows marked release blocker; 131 false.
findings.impact: Mostly non-functional CLI vs reference.
findings.root_cause: Integration seams on nearly every command.
findings.recommended_remediation: Implement per command over the wired crates.

findings.title: Non-TTY fallback exits 0 while doing nothing; reference reads piped stdin as the prompt
evidence: Prints 'starting TUI (requires a TTY)' and exits 0; reference reads piped stdin as initial prompt.
findings.impact: Scripted `echo hi | opencode` silently does nothing.
findings.recommended_remediation: Implement stdin-as-prompt path.

findings.title: Auth login echoes API keys; OAuth login absent from the binary
evidence: API key echoed during auth login (Medium per agent 09); no OAuth login in the binary; Bedrock SigV4/Vertex ADC unimplemented.
findings.impact: Key exposure on shared terminals; provider coverage gaps.
findings.recommended_remediation: Mask keys; add OAuth flows.

findings.title: Telemetry: the port makes no startup network calls (more private than reference)
evidence: No posthog/sentry/analytics strings in crates/; no startup network calls; reference pings GitHub releases on TUI start.
findings.impact: None (positive privacy posture).
findings.recommended_remediation: Document the privacy posture.

findings.title: oc-database crate is faithful and would be wire-compatible once connected
evidence: 21 tests pass; DDL byte-parity golden (19 tables, 16 indexes); 38 migrations semantically identical; WAL/FK/busy_timeout match reference.
findings.impact: Positive: persistence layer is high quality.
findings.recommended_remediation: Wire it in (see DB-001).

findings.title: LLM streaming layer is solid at crate level (unicode splitting, tool calls, usage mapping, retries) and only the runner pipeline is blocked
evidence: Mock round-trip: 4-byte emoji split across 1-byte writes decoded intact; two streamed tool calls assembled; usage mapped (inputTokens=42, nonCached=32, cacheRead=10); HTTP 503/429 retries pass.
findings.impact: Positive foundation.
findings.recommended_remediation: Wire the runner to a real stream.
